rationale: 7 of 9 blocking findings (CR-001, CR-002, CR-003, CR-006, CR-007, CR-008, CR-009) are resolved, verified directly against current source in claude.models.ts, claude.plugin.ts, and anthropic-subscription.template.ts. CR-004 (modelSource-based override protection) remains unresolved by an explicit, now-documented user decision to keep the presence-in-catalog check instead; CR-005 (no test for the override path) remains unresolved per the repo's explicit-request-only testing policy. No new high-risk issues were introduced by the fix-up diff, so decision stays request-changes solely on the two intentionally-left-open items.

business_review.item: Goal: CodeMie-proxied Claude always resolves to a current, compatible model per tier (default/haiku/sonnet/opus) without manual code change, mirroring the Codex/Kimi/Copilot pattern
business_review.notes: resolver added and works for the common (unset) case, but explicit-override gating differs from Copilot's modelSource-based pattern, so a default-sourced-but-still-enabled stale model never gets re-ranked; claude.models.ts:306,330-335 vs copilot-cli.models.ts:213-217

business_review.item: Goal: a user's explicit model choice (CLI flag, env var, project/global config) is never silently overridden
business_review.notes: protection is presence-in-catalog based, not modelSource based as specced; roughly holds for the common cases but conflates 'default' with 'explicit' when both are simply non-empty; claude.models.ts:306,330-335

business_review.item: Goal: anthropic-subscription stops forcing its hardcoded model list onto the claude CLI and defers entirely to the CLI's own built-in defaults (no CodeMie catalog to query on that path)
business_review.notes: claude.plugin.ts's new resolver loop runs unconditionally in beforeRun for every provider; when config.codeMieUrl is set for anthropic-subscription (a supported combo, anthropic-subscription.template.ts:117-120), fetchCatalog takes the SSO path and re-populates ANTHROPIC_MODEL/ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL from the CodeMie catalog — claude.plugin.ts:313-322, claude.models.ts:254-288

business_review.item: Goal: no changes to BaseAgentAdapter or any other agent's plugin — Claude-plugin-local plus one provider-template change only
business_review.notes: diff touches only claude.plugin.ts, new claude.models.ts, and anthropic-subscription.template.ts

business_review.item: Non-goal: no change to how Codex, Kimi, Copilot, Pi, or OpenCode resolve models
business_review.notes: no files under those plugins are touched

business_review.item: Non-goal: no new user-facing command or config UI
business_review.notes: no CLI/UI surface changed

business_review.item: Non-goal: no attempt to unify the two hardcoded model sources under one mechanism

business_review.item: Design 2: explicit-override protection reuses the existing modelSource / CODEMIE_MODEL_SOURCE convention, resolving live only when a tier's modelSource is 'default' or the current model is stale/retired even if a source claims it was explicit
business_review.notes: claude.models.ts never reads env.CODEMIE_MODEL_SOURCE or any modelSource concept; it substitutes a presence-in-catalog check (claude.models.ts:306,332-335) that treats any non-empty CODEMIE_*_MODEL env var as explicit, including a base-layer default the user never chose (src/utils/config.ts:1403-1425 unconditionally sets these vars before the provider overlay) — a stale-but-still-enabled default model is never re-ranked, unlike Copilot's modelSource-gated equivalent (copilot-cli.models.ts:174-217). Confirmed still unresolved on this check round by explicit user decision; tradeoff now documented in-code at claude.models.ts:214-224.

business_review.notes: claude.plugin.ts:313 per-tier loop; claude.models.ts TIER_ENV_VAR keyed per tier
